title: Jesu, Shall I Never Be
description: Jesu, Shall I Never Be in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 13 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 355. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, shall I nev-er be Firm-ly ground-ed up-on thee? Nev-er by thy work a-bide, Nev-er in thy wounds re-side?

lines: O how wavering is my mind,
O how quickly doth my heart
Speak into my soul thy name.
May believe, and feel thee nigh;
Plant, and root, and fix in me
All the mind that was in thee;
Settled peace I then shall find;
Anger I no more shall feel,
Perfect love shall cast out fear;
When I feel it fixed within,
I shall have no power to sin;
How shall sin an entrance find?
God so good, so true, so kind;
I shall to the end endure,
Be no more to sin inclined;
To the image of my Lord,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
